October 3, 2026

Trump administration weighs new escalation against Iran as forces build in region

tags: war, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual

President Trump's senior national security team met at Camp David over the weekend, where decisions described as unusual were reportedly made about a possible new major bombing campaign against Iran. An additional aircraft carrier and roughly 10,000 more troops have been moved into the region, and Iran has signalled it would answer any strike with a proportional response. Separate reporting indicates the administration is considering putting ground troops in Iran after the November midterms.

Attempted flyDubai hijacking raises questions over Iran's role

tags: war, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

A flyDubai flight dropped 14,000 feet in 29 seconds in what authorities describe as a hijacking attempt by the co-pilot, before landing in Saudi Arabia. An Israeli passenger with no flying experience is credited with rushing the cockpit and helping to recover the aircraft. President Trump said that if Iran is found to be behind the incident, it will be struck hard; Tehran had said days earlier that Israel would attempt a false-flag operation of this kind.

Whistleblower who exposed Lutnick's Epstein ties dies by suicide

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell, @oafnation_actual

Simon Andriesz, a former British banker who reported Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's undisclosed business relationship with Jeffrey Epstein to the FBI, has died by suicide. Andriesz was a managing director at BGC Group while Lutnick was chief executive, and he described to the BBC how he uncovered evidence of the relationship Lutnick failed to disclose. His death was confirmed by the Transparency Task Force campaign group. People close to him say he had spent years in and out of mental health care while pursuing the case.

Trump expands pre-election payments to voters with $100 checks to seniors

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

President Trump is sending $100 checks to more than 20 million seniors, described as help toward Medicare Part B premiums and drawn from a Medicare Improvement Fund, with delivery expected in the weeks before the midterm elections. The payments follow $500 Obamacare refund checks going to nearly a million people, concentrated in battleground states. Trump has also said every American, including children, will receive a $5,000 check if Republicans win the midterms. Critics characterise the payments as an attempt to buy votes rather than campaign on policy.

House Republicans enter triage mode one month from election day

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

House Republicans have privately acknowledged that holding the chamber is likely impossible with a month until election day. Campaigning in Ohio, President Trump urged voters who dislike the state's gubernatorial and Senate candidates to close their eyes and vote as though he were on the ballot. Signs of eroding Republican turnout are appearing in states Trump carried by double digits, including Alabama, Oklahoma and Ohio.

Justice Department retreats from cases protecting disabled people's community living

tags: politics, legal, health
sources: @aaronparnas

Following a memo withdrawing federal support for community-based housing and services and expanding institutionalisation of homeless people, the Justice Department has abandoned or weakened at least five investigations involving disabled people's rights, according to NBC News. In Florida the department is seeking to roll back a court order it previously won to keep medically fragile children out of nursing homes. In Texas it is walking away from a 16-year lawsuit aimed at helping disabled people live in their communities.

Prosecutor declined to review additional evidence in Cornell assault case

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The New York district attorney who declined to charge seven fraternity members accused of drugging and gang-raping a Cornell student refused to review additional evidence gathered by Cornell police in 2024, according to The New York Times. Prosecutors said the complainant's statement was all they would consider, and on that basis declined to pursue charges or present evidence to a grand jury. Attorney General Letitia James has since been appointed special prosecutor over the investigation. President Trump said he feels bad for the accused because under James they will not get a fair shake, calling her corrupt. The complainant's lawyer says she has faced repeated attempts to unmask her identity and sustained threats and pressure to drop her lawsuit, and that other women have also been targeted.

Report finds Cornell disciplined few of 1,200 reported assault cases

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

More than 1,200 incidents of sexual assault, dating and domestic violence and stalking were reported to Cornell University's Title IX office between 2018 and 2024, according to a USA Today investigation. The university filed disciplinary charges against an accused student in 162 cases and found at least one at fault in 51. Most of those found responsible received sanctions such as probation or training that allowed them to remain on campus; 14 were suspended and seven expelled or dismissed.

Trump posts Senator Tom Cotton's personal phone number over daylight saving vote

tags: politics, privacy
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump published Senator Tom Cotton's cell phone number on Truth Social alongside a lengthy attack on the Arkansas Republican, after Cotton declined to support the Sunshine Protection Act making daylight saving time permanent. Cotton is a close ally of the president and a member of his own party. Attempts to reach Cotton found his voicemail box full.

Taxpayer ad blitz funded with money appropriated for fallen officer memorials

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Money Congress appropriated for memorials to fallen police officers and for border protection measures was redirected to pay for the administration's nationwide advertising campaign, according to new reporting from The Washington Post. The ads include spots styling President Trump in religious and cinematic terms. The campaign is also funded by taxpayer money more broadly.

Homeland Security bought five planes from a donor at a markup hours before Noem's exit

tags: politics, immigration
sources: @aaronparnas

Hours before Kristi Noem left her post, her agency purchased five planes from a department donor at a significant markup, spending more than $100 million, according to The New York Times. The aircraft were intended to carry deportees but have largely sat idle, with most having flown no deportation flights. The purchase has been cited as an example of the waste the Department of Government Efficiency was meant to eliminate.

Nearly 1,400 laid off at Ohio truck plant days before Trump rally

tags: economy, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

About 1,400 workers were laid off at a truck factory in the greater Dayton area three days before President Trump's rally in Ohio. The cuts erased roughly a year of job growth for the region, according to PBS, which reports manufacturing employment is declining sharply and that such layoffs are hitting these communities hardest. Some remaining factory workers say the layoffs are pushing them to vote Democratic in November.

Appeals court throws out sentence after judge watched AI video of victim

tags: legal, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

The Arizona Court of Appeals has vacated a 10-year manslaughter sentence because the trial judge considered an AI-generated video in which the deceased victim appeared to address the court. The victim's family created the video using his likeness to give him a voice at sentencing. The appeals court held that the video did not convey direct statements from the victim and violated the defendant's due process rights, ordering a resentencing. It is described as the first known use of an AI-generated video of a victim at sentencing.

Satellite imagery shows scale of destruction across Gaza

tags: war, politics
sources: @groundnews

New satellite imagery added to Google Earth shows widespread destruction across Gaza after nearly three years of war, including large sections of Rafah, Khan Younis and Gaza City reduced to rubble. A June 2026 assessment by the United Nations Satellite Centre found about 201,290 structures, or 82% of the territory's total, had sustained damage, with 134,422 classified as destroyed and an estimated 328,627 homes affected. Gaza's Health Ministry says 74,022 Palestinians have been killed since the war began, which followed the Oct. 7, 2023 attack in which Hamas-led militants killed about 1,200 people in Israel and took 251 hostages.

Trump declines to endorse Netanyahu before Israeli election

tags: politics, war
sources: @groundnews

In a 75-minute interview with Time magazine, President Trump deflected repeated questions about whether Israelis should return Benjamin Netanyahu to office ahead of Israel's Oct. 27 election, saying only that he is not involved in politics anymore. The absence of an endorsement is a setback for the Likud leader, who has campaigned on his relationship with Trump. Netanyahu faces a long-running corruption trial, fallout from his 2023 judicial overhaul plan and criticism over security failures before the Oct. 7 attack. The seven-month Iran war has strained the relationship, with Trump objecting to an Israeli strike on an Iranian gas field and calling Netanyahu crazy in June.

Iowa Republican avoids constituents pressing on Epstein files release

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Representative Mariannette Miller-Meeks of Iowa was recorded moving away from constituents confronting her over her refusal to back the release of the Epstein files. She has not signed the discharge petition for the Epstein Files Transparency Act, nor a second discharge petition on the matter. She is running in one of the closest congressional races in the country.

Trump administration moves to repeal roadless rule covering 45 million acres

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

The administration is seeking to eliminate protections that since 2001 have kept new roads and logging out of roughly 45 million acres of national forest, including about 4 million acres in Utah. Officials describe the repeal as a wildfire prevention measure, but opponents note fires are four times more likely to start near a road and that the existing rule already permits thinning and firefighting. The rule also protects more than 80,000 miles of river and watersheds supplying drinking water to over 25 million people, and its removal would open more than 58 million acres to commercial logging and development. A public comment period closes Oct. 6, and polling cited by opponents finds three in four voters, including most Republicans, want the rule kept.

Carbon County to discuss proposed nuclear-powered data center on public lands

tags: tech, climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

The Carbon County Planning Commission meets Oct. 6 at 4:30 p.m. in Price, Utah, to discuss and possibly vote on a proposed data center, followed by a presentation on an associated nuclear project on public lands. No public comment period is expected at the meeting. Residents living near the proposed site are urging community members to attend and report back, and advocates are seeking a future opportunity for public comment.

White House monitors suspected pneumonic plague outbreak in Siberia

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Russian authorities have quarantined nearly 200 people after a woman who worked at an anti-plague research facility in Siberia died of what Russian media report as suspected pneumonic plague, with health authorities still working to confirm the diagnosis. Residents report masks being distributed in kindergartens, protective suits in the streets, hospitals under quarantine and universities considering cancelling classes. Axios reports the Trump administration is aware of the outbreak, monitoring it and assessing options. There is no indication of spread beyond the affected area.

Mass shooting at Georgia homecoming block party kills two and injures dozens

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A gunman opened fire at about 1:20 a.m. at a homecoming block party in Vienna, Georgia, killing two people and injuring roughly 35. Dooly County Sheriff Craig Peavey said about 25 people were taken to hospital. According to the Gun Violence Archive there have been more than 350 mass shootings in the United States so far this year, more than the number of days elapsed.

Tomato tariffs push restaurants toward ending free chips and salsa

tags: economy, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Texas International Produce Association and the Texas Restaurant Association have warned that tomato prices have become too expensive for restaurants to keep absorbing, putting complimentary chips and salsa at risk. A 17% tariff imposed last year on Mexican tomatoes is the main driver, compounded by poor weather in growing regions such as Florida. Restaurants had continued the practice despite rising costs.

Argentina's poverty rate rises to 32% in first increase under Milei

tags: economy, politics
sources: @groundnews

Argentina's statistics agency INDEC reported that 32.3% of the population lived in poverty in the first half of 2026, up from 28.2% in the prior period and the first rise since President Javier Milei brought inflation under control. The rate had fallen from a peak of 52.9% in the first half of 2024. The Catholic University of Argentina projects 35% by year-end. Analysts say gains from slower inflation may be fading and that further progress depends on job creation and real wage growth, while a September AtlasIntel survey put disapproval among lower-income respondents near 70%, up from 57% a year earlier.

Algeria makes forest arson punishable by death after wildfire surge

tags: legal, climate
sources: @groundnews

Algeria's national assembly passed a bill making arson of forests or fields punishable by death, following more than 100 fires in the northeast during a heatwave. Civil Protection recorded 3,719 wildfires between May 1 and July 20, up from 1,501 in the same period of 2025. Justice Minister Lotfi Boudjemaa said arson had reached the level of organised crime and that investigations pointed to ties with foreign parties. Algeria has not carried out an execution since 1993; the law also extends capital punishment to child kidnappings involving torture, sexual assault or mutilation.

California puts $7.5 billion science and health research bond on 2028 ballot

tags: politics, health, climate
sources: @groundnews

Governor Gavin Newsom signed a bill placing a $7.5 billion bond measure on the March 2028 ballot to create the California Foundation for Science and Health Research, which would fund public health, climate science, agriculture and other research through grants and loans. The proposal follows federal research cuts, including nearly $2 billion in cancelled University of California grants beginning in 2025, much of which a court later restored. The measure is a scaled-down version of an earlier $23 billion plan that failed to reach the ballot.

California bans sale of single-use battery-powered vapes

tags: climate, health, politics
sources: @groundnews

Governor Gavin Newsom signed a law outlawing the sale of single-use, battery-powered vapes in California as part of an effort to reduce plastic waste. From Jan. 1, 2027 companies may no longer make or import new or refurbished vapor devices with built-in batteries, and retailers must stop selling them on Jan. 1, 2028, with fines rising from $500 to $2,000 for repeat offences. CalPIRG estimates Americans discard close to 500,000 disposable vapes each day, where batteries can start landfill fires or leach lead and lithium. Business groups opposed the measure, warning of smuggling and strain on family-owned stores.

Physician alleges fraud and harmful protocols in hospital COVID response

tags: health, politics
sources: @ericmoutsos

A former staff surgeon and ICU provider said hospital leadership inflated reported COVID infections and deaths, recorded trauma deaths as COVID deaths, and circulated misleading information about remdesivir after it was supplied by federal authorities. The account alleges the hospital never faced equipment or staffing shortages while headlines described it as overwhelmed, and that nurses were sent home for lack of patients. It also claims the head of infectious disease medicine said he was working with state government to restrict the civil rights of unvaccinated people, including driving, and that primary and urgent care physicians refused to treat unvaccinated patients with the chief medical officer's approval. The physician says disciplinary action was brought against them after raising these concerns.

Heritage Foundation's three decades of advocacy for Netanyahu documented

tags: politics, media
sources: @total.hypocrisy

The Heritage Foundation published an executive memorandum titled "Give Netanyahu a Chance" in 1996 and has promoted his positions to lawmakers and the executive branch in the 30 years since. A search of the foundation's website returns 157 results for Netanyahu. The same organisation produced Project 2025, has figures in the current cabinet, and was the venue through which JD Vance was introduced to Peter Thiel and subsequently to Donald Trump.

Trump says Obama is more corrupt than Nixon

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

President Trump posted on Truth Social that former President Barack Obama is more corrupt than Richard Nixon. The claim comes as Trump's Justice Department seeks to recast Watergate, asserting that Nixon was railroaded and the scandal was a setup. Trump is the only one of the three presidents to have been convicted of a criminal offence; Nixon was pardoned before charges could be brought.

Trump's Ohio rally remarks on aspirin and data centers draw scrutiny

tags: politics, health
sources: @aaronparnas

At a rally in Ohio, President Trump described taking a far larger aspirin dose than his doctors recommend, saying they want him near 80 milligrams while he takes roughly 300, and that he needs it psychologically. He also claimed to know more about inflation than anyone else, singled out an audience member as a housewife with a natural instinct for business, and suggested that opposition to data centers is a Chinese psychological operation. The data center remark drew a quiet response from the crowd.

Singapore launches state matchmaking service amid record-low birth rate

tags: politics, health
sources: @groundnews

Singapore has launched FirstDate, a state-run matchmaking service open to government employees aged 21 to 35, as the city-state faces a record-low fertility rate. Users log in through the national digital identity system, complete a survey and are paired one date at a time using the Gale-Shapley stable marriage algorithm. Fewer than 30,000 babies were born in Singapore in 2025, the lowest in 60 years, with a total fertility rate of 0.87 against a replacement level of 2.1. Critics say the scheme excludes non-government workers and that the age cap shows it targets the birth rate rather than companionship.

AI decompilation tools fuel wave of unauthorised video game mash-ups

tags: tech, legal
sources: @groundnews

Amateur coders are using AI tools to decompile commercial video games and build playable crossovers, with viral examples combining Minecraft with Elden Ring, SKATE with Call of Duty and Escape From Tarkov with Skyrim. IGN reports the trend surged after Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 with cheaper tokens and improved coding ability, letting users with little programming experience direct AI agents to break games into source code. Critics cite copyright concerns, buggy generated code and effects on traditional modding, and it is unclear whether the projects support extended gameplay.
